page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n4 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel x86_64 cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The Intel processor includes advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated mathematical and cryptographic computations.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a clear performance profile characterized by moderate single-core capabilities but constrained multi-core and memory bandwidth performance. Single-core metrics, such as the Geekbench single-core score of 1868.0 and stress-ng single-core CPU performance of 1564.68, fall within the average range. However, multi-core execution is relatively weak, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 4154.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 5956.49. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read and write speeds of 33.17 GB/sec and 21.19 GB/sec respectively, placing it in the bottom quartile of tested systems.

Given the high memory density relative to processing power, the n4-highmem-4 is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring substantial memory footprints without intensive parallel processing demands. It is suited for moderate database operations, text processing, and static web serving, where its 7.0 GB/sec web serving throughput is highly functional. However, it is less suitable for heavy multi-threaded compilation, complex ray tracing, or large-scale LLM inference due to its lower multi-core and memory bandwidth performance.
